findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Require the runbook's format step to re-assert, at execution time, that the target volume is raw (blkid empty) AND matches the expected NVMe serial vol06780b8557d1416b7 immediately before mkfs, aborting with a DATA LOSS RISK note if a filesystem is present.
evidence: The plan's own AC5 discussion states 'auto-mkfs on a volume that merely looks blank is how a restored backup is destroyed, so the unsafe half is exactly the half needed' — acknowledging mkfs as a data-loss vector.
AC1 proves outcome ('mountpoint -q and lsblk showing the fstype') but specifies no pre-mkfs emptiness/identity re-check.
blkid showing 'no filesystem at all' was measured on 2026-09-05; mkfs at execution time relies on that stale reading unless re-verified.
The runbook infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md that holds the ordered procedure does not yet exist in the repo, so its per-step guards are unverifiable from the plan.
findings.finding: The remediation's mkfs step is an irreversible, single-shot destructive operation, but neither AC1 nor the plan text requires the manual runbook to RE-ASSERT the target device is genuinely raw/unformatted immediately before formatting; the raw state was measured once at report time and could differ at execution (e.g., a wrong device, or a volume that was formatted/restored in the interim).
findings.location: Acceptance criteria AC1 ([non-codebase] format + fstab + mount) and 'Remediation is NOT a simple mount' section
scenarios: Operator runs the runbook days later against /dev/nvme2n1, but the device enumeration has shifted or the volume was re-provisioned, and mkfs silently destroys a now-populated filesystem.
A partial earlier remediation left a filesystem on the volume; mkfs overwrites it with no back-out.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a pre-mkfs guard to AC1 / the runbook: `blkid /dev/nvmeXn1` must return empty and `lsblk -o SERIAL` must equal vol06780b8557d1416b7 before formatting; if either fails, abort and do not mkfs.
